rationale: Author-of-record walk of plan §Bead 6's seven steps against 482bcd2f: steps 1 (gitutil primitives), 2 (eight executor seams; no production gitutil import in internal/complete), 3 (validate snapshot legs beside untouched committed-range functions), 4 (Run()'s reconcile-first -> discriminator -> panel-gate-skipped-on-resume -> unified snapshot flow, terminal clear on both completion paths), 5 (ADR-0041 §1 replacement — I verified both stale sentences existed in the pre-image in whitespace-normalized form and are gone, so TestADR0041OQ1a_OldGatesAfterCommitClaimGone would genuinely fire on revert), and 7 (all twenty legs present by name, real-git, green locally: internal/complete 36.7s ok, gitutil/executor/validate ok) are delivered faithfully, and the vacated AC-6 pathspec sentence and AC-7(ii)-(iv) legs are correctly NOT implemented. Step 6 is only half-delivered: AC-7(i) exists (leg xi, real panel, stale-SHA block), but the composed AC-6 fixture — panel-pass at SHA A + dirty tracker + doc-sync-failing change, run 1 refusing at doc-sync with tip still A, run 2 with --allow-doc-skew decided by doc-sync and never stale-SHA — does not exist anywhere (TestRun_DocSyncRefusesBeforeAnyMaterialization is mock-level run-1 only; leg (i) asserts tip-unchanged on the adr-divergence lane with no panel; C2/C3 explicitly register no panel). AC-6 is the bead's headline acceptance criterion and the retry-convergence half is the whole point of #186, so this alone forces REQUEST_CHANGES. Additionally: the ADR text describes the plan-literal S ordering rather than the delivered deviation-C ordering; --commit-msg text is now silently discarded; and materialize.go's comment cites a stage-constants pinning test that does not exist while the resume router's else-catchall would route an unrecognized Mindspec-Stage value down the D-resume path (skipping panel and content gates). The machinery itself is sound and the fixes are all completable without redesign — no hard block.

deviation_assessments.A: NOT acceptable as-is, though the implementer was faithful: the frozen 4-arg MaterializeStageCommit seam is the plan's own literal list, so this is a plan gap, not implementer invention. But silently discarding the operator's --commit-msg text (it now survives only as the permission signal for committing user dirt, never landing in any commit — verified: materializationInput.commitMsg is read only in the dirt guards) is a real audit-trail and honesty loss in a spec named lifecycle-verb-state-honesty: the flag promises a commit message and drops it without a word. The remediation is cheap because gitutil.MaterializeStageCommit ALREADY takes a subject parameter — only the executor seam pinched it off. Thread the message through as the M-stage subject (one added seam parameter, disclosed), or at minimum warn when a provided message is discarded and document the new behavior.
deviation_assessments.B: Acceptable ONLY as coupled with C, which is how it was disclosed. The frozen eight-method seam list genuinely precluded the plan's scoped 'C's tree + refreshed artifact blob' D-construction from inside internal/complete (the only tree-producing seam is SnapshotWorktreeTree), so the full re-snapshot was forced. Residual worth recording: the plan's scoped construction made it impossible BY CONSTRUCTION for non-artifact content to enter D; the delivered form narrows that to a small in-process TOCTOU window between the pre-S classification and the tree2 snapshot (R3/R6's lenses probe its width). The defensive post-D re-check cannot catch a sweep that already landed in D (the worktree then matches D). Acceptable for this bead provided the ADR documents the delivered construction and window (see concrete change 3); a ninth scoped-refresh seam is a legitimate follow-up candidate.
deviation_assessments.C: ACCEPTED on invariant-preservation merits. Given B, the plan's literal check-AFTER-the-S-commit ordering demonstrably violates the plan's own invariant: S's add -A re-snapshot cannot distinguish the artifact refresh from an interval edit once R's reset has run, so the edit would be swept into D before any check saw it — legs (viii-a)/(ix) found this empirically, exactly as disclosed. The delivered ordering (primary classification BEFORE the D snapshot at materialize.go:276-282, refusing via sExitGenuineDirtRefusal with named paths, no rollback, no re-panel, before any merge/worktree-removing path; defensive re-check after in sExitContract) preserves interval-edits-preserved-or-refused-never-silently-committed and strengthens it — the refusal now precedes even D's creation. The S-exit contract's letter (refuse genuine dirt before any merge path that can force-remove the worktree) is kept. The one defect is documentary: ADR-0041 still narrates the plan-literal ordering (concrete change 3).

concrete_changes_required: Add the composed AC-6 fixture plan §Bead 6 step 6 demands (currently absent — verified across bead6_fixture_legs_test.go, complete_test.go, fault_injection_realgit_test.go; C2/C3 explicitly register no panel): real-git fixture with a panel registered at reviewed SHA A + dirty tracker + doc-sync-failing change; run 1 refuses at doc-sync with `git rev-parse` asserting the bead tip is STILL A; run 2 with --allow-doc-skew is decided by doc-sync — never by the panel stale-SHA gate. This is the bead's headline retry-convergence AC (the #186 mechanism) and only its two halves exist separately today.

Deviation A remediation: stop silently discarding --commit-msg. Preferred: pass the operator's message through as the M-stage commit's subject (gitutil.MaterializeStageCommit already accepts a subject; widen the MaterializeStageCommit executor seam by one string parameter and disclose the seam-list deviation). Minimum acceptable: emit a WARN when a provided --commit-msg is not used, and document the fixed-subject behavior in the flag's help text.

Make ADR-0041 describe the DELIVERED mechanism (the BRIEF's own bar for load-bearing deviation C): §1's S bullet ('with a final S-exit dirt re-classification') and §3(i)'s 'S — build commit D ..., then the S-exit dirt contract' narrate the plan-literal post-D ordering. Amend both to state (a) the primary dirt classification runs BEFORE the S-stage snapshot and refuses pre-D, with the post-D re-check as defensive only, and (b) D's tree is a full worktree re-snapshot (not scoped artifact-blob surgery), safe because of (a), including the narrowed-not-eliminated in-run window. Extend the pinning test with an anchor for the pre-snapshot ordering so the doc cannot drift back.

Add the stage-constants pinning test that materialize.go:34-36 already cites as existing ('see materialize_stage_constants_test.go' — no such file): pin internal/complete's duplicated stageMaterialization/stageArtifactSync strings equal to gitutil.StageMaterialization/StageArtifactSync. The duplication is load-bearing for resume routing.

Refuse or foreign-classify an unrecognized Mindspec-Stage value instead of the current else-catchall: runMaterialization (materialize.go:258) routes ANY non-empty resumeStage other than 'materialization' down the artifact-sync D-resume path, and the discriminator returns whatever string the trailer carries — a marker at tip with an unknown stage value (crafted, or a future-version writer) would skip the panel gate AND the content gates via the S-resume route. Validate stage ∈ {materialization, artifact-sync} in resolveMaterializationDiscriminator; unknown → clear marker + normal run (same as the trailer-absent foreign case).

Minor, per the bead's own every-read-propagates hazard: materialize.go:302 discards ReadStageMarker's error when computing D's expectedOld (silently degrades to CREATE semantics), and resolveMaterializationDiscriminator:100 discards the oid^ resolution error (falls through to FOREIGN and deletes the write-ahead marker on a read failure). Both currently fail closed via the CAS/re-measure, but propagate the errors.

Locally re-ran the twenty legs (ok, 36.7s), the ADR pinning tests (ok), and the gitutil/executor/validate suites (ok).
